result.reason: The redline reaches the fallback position: inspections are capped at once per 12 months, require 30 days’ written notice (more protective than the fallback’s 15 days), occur during business hours, and remain entirely at HDI’s cost (more protective than allowing cost-shifting for underpayment above 10%). Because the fallback does not require an independent auditor, confidentiality undertaking, or express prohibition on system access, omitting those preferred-position protections does not prevent compliance. The amendment is narrowly limited to the missing frequency cap and preserves the existing commercial scope. Drafting is clear, though the inherited formulation “may ... have the right” is somewhat awkward.
